title: Batch & Cache Decision Tree Explorer — compact assistant for tradeoffs
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Design a compact, step-driven Decision Tree Explorer inside the Redwood Console that helps engineers and platform owners choose batching + caching configurations for a given workload. The experience is intentionally light-weight (single-panel compact overlay) and focuses on: 1) surfacing recommended presets based on workload signals (median latency target, request size profile, prefix reuse rate), 2) explaining trade-offs in plain language and visual micro-summaries (cost delta, p99 latency risk), and 3) attaching guardrails with quick rollback and explainable reasons for automated suggestions. This ticket covers low-fidelity flows, annotated microcopy, internal prototype for engineering handoff, and a short usability validation with two internal platform engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Compact overlay UI with a 3-step guided flow: workload signals -> recommendation -> applied policy preview
Recommendation cards include expected cost delta, expected p50/p95 latency change, and confidence score
Copy and micro-visuals explain one trade-off per decision (e.g., higher batching reduces unit cost but may increase token-level tail latency)
Guardrail toggle with immediate explainable reasons and a one-click rollback path is shown in preview
Annotated handoff spec (Figma + props table) delivered for ENG with documented inputs for simulator and API contract

design_decisions: Use a compact single-panel overlay rather than a full page to reduce context-switch for on-call operators
Signal-first flow (ingest workload metrics -> present recommended presets) performed best in early walkthroughs
Show cost delta as both percentage and absolute $/100k tokens to make economics accessible to non-financial readers
Include a confidence score derived from historical match-rate of similar workloads; surface uncertainty with an inline tooltip
Guardrails are visible by default but require explicit enable to apply automated rollouts
usability_findings: Participants preferred an explicit 'why this recommendation' line over raw charts when under time pressure
Number formatting matters: testers favored '2.3% cost reduction (~$0.14/100k tokens)' vs only percentages
One tester requested simulated tail-latency examples for high-batch presets; add micro-scenario toggles in next prototype
Confusion arose around prefix-KV caching semantics; added microcopy explaining 'prefix reuse rate' and an 'example trace' link
